name: Short Rib-Polydactyly Syndrome Type 5

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Short Rib-Polydactyly Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of markedly shortened ribs resulting in narrow thorax
Postaxial polydactyly of hands and/or feet
Characteristic radiographic findings including short long bones with metaphyseal abnormalities
Presence of visceral anomalies such as cystic dysplastic kidneys or hepatic fibrosis
Genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants in associated ciliopathy genes (e.g., DYNC2H1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis requires presence of all three major criteria: narrow thorax due to short ribs, postaxial polydactyly, and characteristic radiographic skeletal abnormalities.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory. Differential diagnosis includes other short rib-polydactyly syndromes and related ciliopathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Markedly shortened ribs causing narrow thoracic cage
searchTerms: very short ribs causing narrow chest

pathognomonic.symptomName: Postaxial polydactyly of hands and/or feet
searchTerms: extra fingers or toes on pinky side
additional digits near little finger or toe

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe micromelia with short long bones

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to restrictive thoracic cage
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to chest size
kidneys with cysts and abnormal structure

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac malformations such as ventricular septal defect

searchTerms: facial abnormalities with cleft lip or palate
split lip or roof of mouth

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes in hepatic fibrosis
Renal function abnormalities in cystic dysplastic kidneys
imaging: Radiographs showing short ribs and narrow thorax
Skeletal survey revealing micromelia and metaphyseal abnormalities
Ultrasound demonstrating cystic kidneys and hepatic fibrosis
other: Prenatal ultrasound showing narrow thorax and polydactyly
Postmortem findings in lethal cases include pulmonary hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Type 1 has more severe thoracic constriction and distinct facial features

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress in neonatal period
Markedly narrow thoracic cage on imaging
Presence of postaxial polydactyly with skeletal abnormalities
references: Beales PL, et al. Short rib-polydactyly syndromes: clinical and molecular genetics. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2011.
Mickelson EC, et al. The ciliopathies: an expanding disease spectrum. Pediatr Clin North Am. 2014.
Orphanet Report Series: Short rib-polydactyly syndrome type 5. Orphanet. 2023.
